extracted.intended_audience: measure developers, hospital quality staff, CMS stakeholders, and commenters responding to CMS proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria used by CMS and the Partnership for Quality Measurement (PQM) to evaluate, endorse, and maintain clinical quality measures (e.g., EDAC, diabetes measures) during pre‑rulemaking and measure implementation. Includes procedural voting rules, model performance thresholds, cohort eligibility, reporting/attestation requirements, and standardization expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑Rulemaking Measure Review voting process and consensus threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation Group members will vote to either “recommend” or “do not recommend” that a measure be added to the intended CMS program(s); the “recommend with conditions” option was removed in 2025. The threshold to reach consensus on a given measure is a minimum of 75 percent agreement among members. Recommendation Group members can provide considerations for CMS to review prior to implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rule for how PQM Recommendation Groups decide on measure recommendations during the pre‑rulemaking cycle; informs whether a measure proceeds toward CMS programs and what input can accompany a recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model discriminant ability (c‑statistic) interpretation and threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The c‑statistic indicates a model's discriminant ability to correctly classify patients who have and have not had a qualifying event within 30 days; values range from 0.5 (no better than chance) to 1.0 (perfect prediction). The CBE has determined that for readmission‑type measures, a c‑statistic of 0.68 is considered an effective model of discriminant ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the c‑statistic as a core indicator of model discrimination; target ≥0.68 for readmission‑type measures. Refer to the Diabetes EDAC Risk Adjustment and Model Performance Testing documentation for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive ability (decile range of observed outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive ability measures the ability to distinguish high‑risk subjects from low‑risk subjects. A model with good predictive ability would see a wide range in observed outcomes between lowest and highest deciles of predicted outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess predictive performance by calculating the range of mean observed hospital ratios between the lowest and highest deciles of predicted hospital visit probabilities; greater separation indicates better predictive utility. See measure‑specific model performance reports (e.g., Diabetes EDAC) for examples and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort inclusion rule for Veterans Health Administration (VHA) beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: VHA beneficiaries hospitalized in VHA hospitals are eligible for inclusion in the cohort regardless of their Medicare enrollment status. VHA beneficiaries hospitalized in non‑VHA hospitals must be concurrently enrolled in Medicare Fee‑For‑Service Part A or Medicare Advantage at the time of the index admission to be eligible for cohort inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this enrollment‑based eligibility exception when constructing cohorts for measures that rely on Medicare enrollment data to determine inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for Maternal Morbidity Structural Measure (two‑part question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals respond to a two‑part question: “Does your hospital or health system participate in a Statewide and/or National Perinatal Quality Improvement Collaborative Program aimed at improving maternal outcomes during inpatient labor, delivery and postpartum care, and has it implemented patient safety practices or bundles related to maternal morbidity to address complications, including, but not limited to, hemorrhage, severe hypertension/preeclampsia or sepsis?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two‑part attestation captures both participation in collaborative quality improvement efforts and implementation of specific safety practices/bundles; further details are found in the FY 2022 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule and in the QualityNet attestation guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z‑score standardization for hospital performance comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Z‑score standardization translates hospital results into a common scale, indicating how each hospital's performance compares with the overall average, helping reduce the impact of extreme values and differences in scoring methods while supporting fair and consistent comparisons across hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use z‑score standardization when reporting and comparing hospital performance metrics to improve fairness and comparability across facilities and scoring methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure removal factors (IQR Program removal criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal factors for the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program are summarized in prior IPPS/LTCH PPS final rules and are codified at 42 CFR 412.140(g)(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether a measure should be continued or removed, refer to the removal factors codified in regulation and summarized in the cited final rules; these factors inform removal decisions during measure maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability guidance requirement for endorsement and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer readers to the Reliability Guidance for the Endorsement and Maintenance of Clinical Quality Measures Document for details on reliability testing and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures submitted for endorsement or maintenance should meet the reliability standards and testing approaches in the Reliability Guidance document; see PQM resources for specifics on acceptable reliability evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized value sets (Value Set Authority Center / VSAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: To access the value sets for the measure, please visit the Value Set Authority Center (VSAC) sponsored by the National Library of Medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should reference and use standardized value sets from VSAC to ensure consistent concept definitions and interoperability across implementers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation/web‑based data collection requirement for structural measures
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS QualityNet IQR Measures—Web‑Based Data Collection: Attestation Guide for the Maternal Morbidity Structural Measure provides the instructions for hospitals to attest to meeting structural measure criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals reporting structural measures must follow the QualityNet attestation process and guidance when submitting web‑based attestations; consult the QualityNet attestation guide for required fields and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and documentation of readmission algorithm and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Details regarding the planned readmission algorithm and condition‑specific EDAC methodology are available on the CMS Measure Methodology site and in measure‑specific reports (e.g., EDAC Measures Updates and Specifications Report, Risk Adjustment and Model Performance Testing zip files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure developers and reviewers should provide transparent algorithm documentation and model/methodology files in publicly accessible locations (e.g., CMS Measure Methodology, PQM zip files) so stakeholders can evaluate specifications, risk adjustment, and performance testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model performance and risk adjustment documentation requirement (EDAC example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures such as Diabetes EDAC include Risk Adjustment and Model Performance Testing documentation that report c‑statistics, predictive ability, and other model performance metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive risk adjustment and performance testing reports as part of measure submission and pre‑rulemaking materials; reviewers will evaluate discriminant ability, calibration, predictive separation, and other model diagnostics.
